description: Experience the exhilarating flavors of a classic Chinese Hot and Sour Soup, a perfect balance of tangy vinegar, fiery chili, and savory umami. This comforting and aromatic dish, brimming with tender tofu, mushrooms, and bamboo shoots, is a staple in Chinese cuisine. Prepare to warm your soul and tantalize your taste buds with every spoonful of this delightful homemade rendition.

instructions.title: Prepare Ingredients
instructions.text: Rehydrate dried shiitake and wood ear mushrooms in hot water for 20-30 minutes, then drain, squeeze dry, and thinly slice. Cut pork into thin strips and tofu into cubes. Prepare cornstarch slurry by mixing cornstarch with 3 tablespoons of water.

instructions.title: Cook Pork and Broth
instructions.text: In a large pot, bring chicken or vegetable broth to a boil. Add the thinly sliced pork and cook for 2-3 minutes until no longer pink. Skim any foam that rises to the surface.

instructions.title: Add Vegetables and Seasonings
instructions.text: Add sliced shiitake mushrooms, wood ear mushrooms, and julienned bamboo shoots to the broth. Stir in soy sauce, rice vinegar, and white pepper. Bring the soup back to a gentle simmer.

instructions.title: Thicken the Soup
instructions.text: Slowly pour the cornstarch slurry into the simmering soup in a thin stream, stirring constantly, until the soup thickens to your desired consistency. Continue to simmer for 1-2 minutes to cook out the cornstarch taste.

instructions.title: Add Tofu and Egg
instructions.text: Gently add the cubed firm tofu to the soup. Slowly drizzle the beaten egg into the simmering soup in a thin stream, stirring gently in one direction with a ladle or chopsticks to create delicate egg ribbons.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the soup from heat. Stir in sesame oil and chili oil. Taste and adjust seasonings if necessary, adding more vinegar, pepper, or chili oil to your preference. Ladle into bowls and garnish with chopped green onions before serving hot.

tips: For authentic texture, use good quality rice vinegar and white pepper. The white pepper provides a unique pungency that defines the 'hot' in Hot and Sour Soup, distinct from chili heat.
To ensure a smooth, lump-free thickening, always create a cornstarch slurry with cold water before adding it to hot soup, and pour it in slowly while stirring constantly.
Adjust the 'hot' and 'sour' elements to your personal preference. Add more rice vinegar for extra tang and more chili oil or white pepper for increased heat.
